A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research project, sharing authors, neighboring-knowledge retention, and sliced-Wasserstein regularization despite extensive revision and renaming. All main-text pages, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original unlearning and benchmark experiments on Llama2 and Mistral, ablations, batch/sequential experiments, human evaluation, and qualitative model outputs.

after.justification: v2 reports original ELUDe experiments on Llama-3.1 and Phi-3.5, regularization and retention analyses, adversarial and membership-inference evaluations, and human dataset evaluation.

M1.justification: SNAP trains on generated refusal responses; OPT-OUT instead applies reference-model negative preference optimization to factual forget examples, alongside retention training. Data construction changes from free-form GPT-4/GPT-3.5 generation to Wikipedia-grounded GPT-4o QA with explicit neighboring-entity selection. The sliced-Wasserstein regularizer remains, but the forgetting objective and construction procedure change substantially.

E1.justification: The Marvel-character and Bill Gates studies give way to ELUDe factual QA about real people: 20 targets are constructed, with main results averaged over five targets. Alpaca-GPT4 replaces Dolly as general instruction data. CommonsenseQA is added, BoolQ and MathQA disappear, and seven benchmarks remain. Nine adversarial scenarios, including cross-lingual prompts, are added; batch/sequential and dedicated multi-hop unlearning evaluations disappear.

E2.justification: v1's main comparison uses Prompting, Euclidean, and Fisher. v2 compares Guardrail, corresponding to Prompting, with GA, DPO, NPO, and IDK, each training method evaluated with and without retention. Fisher disappears. Euclidean regularization reappears in v2 Table 2 alongside newly evaluated Manhattan, Chebyshev, and cosine alternatives.

E3.justification: Refusal-based UA/RA/TA are replaced by FQ/RQ combining probabilities, ROUGE-L, and truth ratios. Backbones change from Llama2-7b/Mistral-7b to Llama-3.1-8B/Phi-3.5-Mini. v1 samples 100 training examples per forget/retain set; v2 specifies an 8:1:1 retain split and 50k/1k/1k world split. Reported weight decay changes from 10% to 0.01. New attack protocols include paraphrase-based membership testing and 900 adversarial samples per entity.

E4.justification: v2 adds membership-inference and nine adversarial-prompt analyses, expands regularization comparisons, and revises the neighboring-data ablation to compare no retention, world data, and world-plus-neighbor data. v1's batch/sequential study and original-versus-unlearned output comparison disappear. Human evaluation now checks passage-based factuality instead of question-type assignment.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix A specifies three random seeds, Tables 1 and 4 report ± variation, and Figure 5 displays standard-deviation bands. v2's main results are averaged over five targets without seed counts or uncertainty estimates; only the MIA table reports means and standard deviations. This substantially changes uncertainty reporting, while v2's actual repeated-run count remains unspecified.

E6.justification: The UA/RA/TA, sequential, and qualitative-output results are replaced by FQ/RQ, attack, and component-metric results. For example, v2 Table 1 reports Llama-3.1 FQ of 87.8 for OPT-OUT versus 82.6 for NPO+RT, both with RQ 46.6. Table 3 adds OPT-OUT MIA accuracies of 48.6% and 49.1%. Different data, backbones, and metrics prevent direct performance comparisons with v1.

T1.justification: v2 adds an explicit entity-specific, disjoint forget/retain-set formulation, GA/NPO loss definitions, and revised FQ/RQ definitions. The central optimal-transport and sliced-Wasserstein mathematics remains equivalent across v1 Equations 2–5 and v2 Equations 4–7. These are limited formal additions without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contributions on negative instructions, appropriate refusal responses, hard retaining data, and applicability to personal or copyrighted knowledge. v2 centers entity-level knowledge removal, claims the first entity-level dataset through ELUDe, and claims superiority over contemporary unlearning methods. Wasserstein-based retention remains a central contribution.

C2.justification: v1 explicitly acknowledges that knowledge remains in the parameters and the model learns to avoid answering. v2 instead asserts parametric knowledge removal while acknowledging gibberish, retention losses, and the absence of evaluations at 70B parameters or above. Its OT explanation also shifts toward selectively allowing changes important for forgetting while preserving parameters important for retention.

D1.justification: Appendix A changes reported hardware from one RTX A6000 to four H100s and documents the NPO temperature and three-epoch early-stopping setup. v1's mixed-precision, checkpointing, ZeRO-2/offload, and approximately two-hour runtime disclosures disappear. v2 adds detailed Wikipedia selection criteria and QA, paraphrasing, perturbation, and attack-generation instructions, while updating the code/data access pointer.

R1.justification: Positioning shifts from knowledge editing and selective generation toward instance-versus-entity unlearning and dataset construction. v2 adds substantive discussion of NPO, TOFU, RWKU, WMDP, and concurrent entity-level work by Ma et al. The earlier discussions of Eldan and Russinovich, R-Tuning, and knowledge-editing approaches are removed.

P1.justification: The title and method terminology change from SNAP to OPT-OUT, with extensive rewriting of the abstract, introduction, methodology, experiments, and limitations. A dedicated Dataset Construction section appears, Related Work moves from Section 2 to Section 5, and the appendices are substantially reorganized.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are substantially redrawn. Separate unlearning and NLP result displays become a joint main table with new metric and model groupings. The dataset pie charts and sequential curve disappear; attack displays, a detailed component-results table, and large prompt/example panels appear. The retaining-data chart changes from two-condition vertical bars to three-condition horizontal bars.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence for knowledge unlearning through correct-answer probabilities, truth-ratio evaluation, contemporary baselines, and adversarial tests, addressing v1's reliance on refusal counts. Wikipedia-grounded QA and the factuality audit also improve the empirical foundation. Reduced uncertainty reporting and removal of sequential and generated-output analyses are meaningful losses, and complete erasure remains unestablished. Nevertheless, the gains in evaluation validity and comparison quality provide a substantial overall improvement.
